picks.headline: Ask the Chefs: AI and Copyright Licensing
picks.excerpt: The US Department of Justice filed a Statement of Interest in the NYT v. OpenAI/Microsoft copyright litigation, largely siding with the AI companies and favoring LLM training as fair use. A panel of publishing experts reacts to what it means for content licensing.
picks.rationale: A full panel of publishing operators saying, on the record, how they will price and structure AI licensing now — the practitioner playbook, not another filing report.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: frame the card on the chefs' licensing answers, NOT on the DOJ Statement of Interest itself — that filing already shipped on 2026-09-15 (books-us-gov-ai-copyright). Use it only as one clause of setup.

picks.headline: Flowtica Verso is an e-Ink AI screen that attaches to your phone
picks.excerpt: The Flowtica Verso's always-on e-paper display sets it apart from standard screenless AI voice recorders, pairing ambient AI capture with an E-Ink reading surface.
picks.rationale: The only hardware release in the pool: an ambient AI recorder that puts an E-Ink reading surface on the phone, a new shape for where reading happens.
picks.cross_section_flag: Possible collision with the gadgets section — verify this URL is not also selected there before roll.

picks.headline: Large Scale Digitization in the AI Era: Model Terms for Libraries and Their AI Partners
picks.excerpt: The Center for Research Libraries has published an issue paper giving libraries concrete contract language for the wave of proposals to digitize their collections at scale for commercial AI training. It covers ownership, permitted uses, public access, compensation and attribution — a negotiating template for anyone whose stacks are being courted as a dataset.
picks.rationale: Replacement pick: actual model contract clauses a librarian or special-collections lead can take into the next digitization-for-AI-training negotiation — the most concretely usable item in the recovery pool, and from an outlet not otherwise in the five.

picks.headline: The Cost of Deepfakes: PW Talks with Meena Kandasamy
picks.excerpt: In the novelist's 'Fieldwork as a Sex Object' (Soft Skull, Nov.), a young Indian woman faces harassment after someone posts a deepfake video of her. Kandasamy discusses writing fiction about synthetic media harm.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the one story about writing synthetic-media harm as fiction rather than litigating it — a craft angle the section has not run.

picks.headline: PW Spotlight: Time to Reclaim the Driver's Seat in AI
picks.excerpt: Bookpact.ai, founded by Sander Ruys, is a licensing platform that lets publishers set per-deal terms, compensation and usage tracking for how AI companies access their titles. (Marked Sponsored / PW Studio content.)
picks.rationale: Concrete per-deal licensing plumbing publishers can actually sign up for — ranked last and labeled because it is PW Studio sponsored content, not newsroom reporting.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: disclose in the body that this is PW Studio sponsored content from bookpact.ai; treat vendor claims as claims.
